title: PharmaRAG-GNN
role: TODO: your role (e.g. author / ml engineer)
summary: explainable hybrid framework integrating knowledge-graph retrieval-augmented generation (rag) with graph neural networks (gnns) to predict drug–drug interactions (ddis).

caseFile.problem: predicting drug–drug interactions (ddis) is critical for clinical safety, yet pure black-box neural models struggle to explain why two compounds interact, while standalone retrieval systems miss structural patterns across pharmacological graphs.
caseFile.approach: combined structured pharmacological knowledge graphs with retrieval-augmented generation and graph neural network message passing. the graph encoder captures molecular and relational topology, while graph-grounded rag retrieves supporting interaction pathways and context.
caseFile.architecture: a dual-pathway pipeline: structured pharmacological triples feed both a gnn interaction predictor and a knowledge-graph retriever, merging structural embeddings with retrieved evidence for explainable ddi predictions.
caseFile.learned: grounding neural predictions in an explicit knowledge graph makes model outputs inspectable rather than opaque, and cleanly separating retrieval from graph inference keeps the system modular.
